skill.name: pptx
skill.description: Create, edit, analyze, validate, and preview PowerPoint PPTX presentations using HTML conversion, OOXML workflows, and helper scripts.
skill.summary: Work with PowerPoint decks through creation, editing, text replacement, validation, and thumbnail review.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Static analysis produced many documentation and schema false positives, especially OOXML URLs, Markdown backticks, and schema regex patterns. Confirmed issues are legitimate local file, archive, subprocess, environment, and sudo dependency behaviors that support PPTX workflows but require sandboxing for untrusted inputs.

remediation.issue: Unsafe archive extraction can allow zip slip paths in malicious Office files.
remediation.suggestion: Replace extractall with a safe extractor that rejects absolute paths, drive prefixes, and members that resolve outside the target directory.

remediation.issue: Dependency instructions include sudo apt-get commands.
remediation.suggestion: Present system packages as manual prerequisites and instruct agents not to run sudo automatically during skill execution.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts invoke external binaries such as soffice, pdftoppm, and git.
remediation.suggestion: Keep shell=False, validate input and output paths, use timeouts consistently, and document that these tools should run in a sandbox for untrusted files.

remediation.issue: The HTML conversion workflow renders local HTML in Chromium.
remediation.suggestion: Disable JavaScript when possible, block network access in the browser context, and only render HTML generated inside the trusted workspace.

semantic_findings.title: Local HTML Rendering Executes Embedded Scripts
semantic_findings.description: The html2pptx helper opens a local HTML file with Playwright using page.goto(file://...). If untrusted HTML is supplied, embedded scripts can execute inside the browser context during conversion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code launches Chromium and loads local HTML. The risk depends on whether user-provided HTML is passed to the helper, but the capability is present.

content.value_statement: PowerPoint work often needs reliable creation, editing, validation, and visual review. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured PPTX workflows with helper scripts for slides, templates, and OOXML.
actual_capabilities: Creates new PPTX decks from HTML slides through the html2pptx and PptxGenJS workflow.
Edits existing PPTX files by unpacking Office Open XML, modifying slide XML, and repacking the archive.
Extracts structured text inventories from presentations for template analysis and replacement planning.
Applies template text replacements while preserving bullets, alignment, fonts, colors, and spacing.
Generates slide thumbnail grids for visual review, layout checks, and template navigation.
Validates edited Office XML against included schemas before producing the final presentation.
limitations: Requires local dependencies such as PptxGenJS, Playwright, Sharp, LibreOffice, Poppler, and python-pptx.
Complex animations, embedded media, and advanced PowerPoint effects may need direct OOXML edits.
Visual accuracy depends on available fonts and the rendering behavior of local conversion tools.
Untrusted PPTX or HTML inputs should be handled in a sandbox because helper scripts process local files.

use_cases.title: Build a New Deck
use_cases.description: Create a styled presentation from an outline, add charts or tables, and validate the final slides visually.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Template
use_cases.description: Inventory a template, duplicate useful slides, replace placeholder text, and preserve the original visual system.

use_cases.title: Repair an Existing PPTX
use_cases.description: Unpack a presentation, inspect OOXML, fix broken slide content, validate the package, and repack the file.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new presentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 6-slide PowerPoint presentation about [topic]. Use a clear visual hierarchy, speaker-friendly slide titles, and a professional color palette.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Presentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for analysis and improvement suggestions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this PPTX file for structure, visual consistency, readability, and missing content. Summarize the main issues and recommend specific slide edits.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that preserves an existing design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this template PPTX to create a new presentation from my outline. Inventory the template, choose matching layouts, replace text, and generate thumbnails for review.

prompt_templates.title: Edit OOXML Directly
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced repair or precision editing workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Modify this PPTX at the OOXML level to change [specific slide elements]. Validate after each edit, repack the file, and report any remaining compatibility risks.

output_examples.input: A request to create a quarterly business review deck from bullet notes and metrics.
output_examples.output: A finished PPTX with section slides, chart placeholders filled, consistent typography, and a thumbnail grid for review.

output_examples.input: A branded template plus replacement text for product launch slides.
output_examples.output: A revised presentation that keeps the template layout, updates the slide copy, and flags any overflow risks.

output_examples.input: A PPTX file that PowerPoint reports as damaged after manual XML edits.
output_examples.output: A repaired deck when possible, plus a concise validation report naming the files and issues that required changes.

best_practices: Inspect the source deck or template before editing so layout, fonts, colors, and slide relationships stay consistent.
Generate thumbnails after changes and check for clipped text, overlap, poor contrast, and missing media.
Validate OOXML immediately after each direct XML edit, then repack only after validation passes.
anti_patterns: Do not edit PPTX zip contents without validating relationships, IDs, namespaces, and content types.
Do not rely on unsupported HTML styling when creating slides through the HTML conversion workflow.
Do not run helper scripts on untrusted presentations or HTML outside a controlled workspace.

faq.question: Can this skill create a PowerPoint deck from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses an HTML-to-PPTX workflow with PptxGenJS to create positioned slides, charts, tables, images, and text.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing PPTX file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can unpack the PPTX archive, edit Office Open XML files, validate the result, and repack the presentation.

faq.question: Does it support branded templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze template text and thumbnails, select suitable layouts, and replace content while preserving formatting.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: Common workflows need Python packages, PptxGenJS, Playwright, Sharp, LibreOffice, Poppler, and MarkItDown for extraction.

faq.question: Can it guarantee exact PowerPoint rendering?
faq.answer: No. Rendering can vary by fonts, local conversion tools, and PowerPoint support for advanced effects.

faq.question: Is it safe to process untrusted PPTX files?
faq.answer: Use a sandbox for untrusted files. The helper scripts unpack archives, render documents, and run local conversion tools.
